rows.quote: Advanced Manufacturing: Advanced Manufacturing students now work and learn in a state-of-the-art machine shop and have the opportunity to earn a number of industry- recognized credentials to demonstrate their technical capacity. All junior students completed the NC3 PMI 6 Certification. These students have six stackable credentials in measuring. The seniors have earned six stackable credentials in Advanced Measuring Instrument this year, which expands upon the PMI credentials into more advanced measuring skills. Over two hundred credentials in metrology were earned. All Freshman students successfully completed safety training earning Career Safe OSHA 10-hour general industry certification. We completed many projects for the community including tags for the Royalston Fire Department, and a plaque for the Town of Ashburnham. Fourteen Seniors and eleven Juniors earned co-op placements, working and learning in area machine shops. (Total student enrollment: 50)

rows.year_basis: fiscal year edition; the school year the page names
rows.quote: Auto Body Collision Repair Technology: Monty Tech Auto Body students earned valuable industry credentials in the 2024- 2025 School year. Students earned the OSHA 10- hour general industry card, EPA 6H spray certification, and ALI Certification. Students also earned I-CAR Certifications in Collision Repair Fundamentals, Disassembly and Re-assembly, Plastic Repair, Aluminum and Steel Small Dent Removal, and Preparation for Refinishing. Seven Seniors and three juniors earned co-op placements and were reported to be valuable contributors to local repair shops in the area. One Junior was placed on externship at the Gardner Fire Dept. At the SkillsUSA District Competition, seven out of nine students won a medal, earning a silver and gold in Auto Refinishing and Collision Repair. Two students were able to attend the SkillsUSA National Competition. We maintained several school vans, and painted multiple railings, stairs, and brackets for our MVP building. We painted a UTV for the Gardner Fire Department, repaired water leaks from a Petersham Police car, and repaired a car for Second Chance Cars to be given to a local family in need. We are currently working on a 1968 Ford Bronco, which will be auctioned off, and all proceeds will be donated to the Teen Challenge of New England. (Total student enrollment: 67)

rows.quote: Automotive Technology: In Automotive Technology we serviced, repaired, and diagnosed approximately three hundred vehicles throughout the year. These jobs included basic maintenance, inspections, alignments, brakes, exhaust, tires, and more. We also serviced the Petersham Police Department vehicle. The Upperclassmen earned their NC3/Snap on Apollo D8 Certification, Juniors earned their NC3/Snap on Multimeter certification, and the freshmen students earned the Career Safe OSHA 10 Certification. Seven Seniors and one junior earned a Co- op placement. For the SkillsUSA Competition, our Junior students placed third and fifteenth. While two Seniors placed fifth and fifteenth in the State Competition. (Total student enrollment: 69)

rows.quote: Business Technology: Monty Tech’s Business Technology program continues to thrive through its financial literacy initiatives. All Juniors and Seniors earned a financial literacy certificate through the MassMutual Foundation FutureSmart program. This year, one student represented the program in the Customer Service competition at the SkillsUSA District level. In addition, four Seniors and seven Juniors secured co-op placements for the 2024–2025 school year. Freshmen and Sophomores successfully completed the Career Safe OSHA 10-hour training and CareerSafe Interview Skills modules. The department also engaged in several collaborative projects: a Macy’s Day Parade project with Information Technology, an Oreo Cookie Redesign project with Culinary and Advanced Manufacturing, and an International Hotel Project with CAD Drafting & Design. Weekly case studies have been introduced to highlight companies, product development, and international relations. These activities foster teamwork, communication, and collaboration both within Business Technology and across other technical areas. (Total student enrollment: 58)

rows.quote: Cabinetmaking: Monty Tech Cabinetmaking students are called upon for a number of projects small and large, across the campus and in our communities. During the 2024- 2025 school year, students completed projects that included: build and install cabinets and countertops for the MVP Academy, build and install cabinets and countertops for the new IT office, and the existing dental shop. A number of projects were made for charitable gifts such as, flag shadow boxes for veterans, a toy box for the Christmas toy drive, and a coat storage unit for the Monty Tech Foundation. Fourteen Seniors & Thirteen Juniors earned co- op placements, representing the program well in the local workforce. Cabinetmaking freshmen completed OSHA Careersafe 10 hr online course. (Total student enrollment: 70)

rows.quote: CAD/Drafting & Design: In 2024- 2025, five Monty Tech CAD/Drafting & Design Senior students and one Junior earned Co-op Placement. Students were also able to achieve a number of valuable industry-recognized certifications including Autodesk Inventor, Revit, Autodesk AutoCAD and SolidWorks. Freshmen students completed the 10hr OSHA CareerSafe Online course. All students earned the Fundamental of Building Green Certifications. Two students competed in the SkillsUSA District Competition. The shop completed a variety of signs, banners, and posters for the school. We collaborated with Business Technology for a hotel design project and website. We designed the addition to the Phillipston Animal Control Facility. (Total student enrollment: 45)

rows.year_basis: fiscal year edition; the school year the page names
rows.quote: Cosmetology: The Monty Tech Cosmetology program is one of the only programs that students may leave and directly enter the industry, fully- licensed and ready for a career. The state- approved program is rigorous and provides students with countless opportunities to refine their cosmetology skills on clientele who understand and appreciate the learning environment. Freshmen completed the Career Safe Online OSHA course. Eighteen senior students earned their cosmetology licenses. Seven students earned Co- op Placement opportunities. One Senior placed Gold in SkillsUSA Districts and went to the SkillsUSA State Competition. Students earned certification in Pravana Color Certification, barbicide, and dermalogica certifications. Two Junior students went to SkillsUSA State Competition. Freshmen and Sophomores participated in Family & Friends Service Day. We participated in Beauty Battles at Worcester Voke, in which several sophomores won 1st & 2nd in nails and 1st in textured hair. One junior placed 1st for formal hair. (Total student enrollment: 85)

rows.quote: Culinary Arts: Monty Tech Culinary Arts students and instructors operate a full-service restaurant and bakery, serving 70-90 patrons daily. In September, they hosted a Welcome Back/New Teachers reception serving hors d’oeuvres and mini pastries for 60 people after school. They prepared a luncheon for Principals & Counselors Day for 30 people in October. They prepared dinner for both Program Advisory Dinner/meetings for over 380 people each time. Students and staff hosted the Westminster Senior Center holiday party for 110 people, funded by the Ryan Patrick Jones Foundation. The program also continued to donate leftover baked goods to the Salvation Army of Fitchburg. Freshmen earned their Career Safe OSHA 10 hour Culinary certification, sophomores & juniors earned their Allergen Awareness certification, and juniors and seniors earned their Servsafe certification. One Senior competed at the state level in the SkillsUSA cooking competition. Junior students toured Johnson & Wales University of Providence RI. Sophomores students went to Great Wolf Lodge in Fitchburg where they toured the property and learned about the hotel industry and career opportunities. (Total student enrollment: 66)

rows.year_basis: fiscal year edition; the school year the page names
rows.quote: Dental Assisting: Monty Tech Dental Assisting instructors have emphasized the need for students to earn valuable industry- recognized credentials, as a means to demonstrate technical skill and proficiency. In 2024- 2025, students obtained their certificate from CDC for Infection Control. Sophomores & Seniors received certification from American Red Cross for Basic Life support, and all freshmen received the Career Safe 10 Hour OSHA. Eight Seniors and seven Juniors earned co- op placements, while the remaining Juniors and Seniors earned experience in affiliation/externship in area dental clinics and offices. Through the Community Health Connections Caring for Kids Program, Monty Tech students could receive free dental cleaning, radiographs, and sealants. Our students were allowed to assist in their procedure. Junior students provided dental education for the pre-school children at the Guild of St. Agnes at Devens and Head Start in Fitchburg. One Senior received a gold medal to go to SkillsUSA states competition. (Total student enrollment: 60)

rows.year_basis: fiscal year edition; the school year the page names
rows.quote: Early Childhood Education: Seven Seniors & eight Juniors earned co- op placements, gaining valuable experience working with young children in local childcare centers. Two Seniors and one Junior gained experience on externships. All Sophomore & Seniors completed their Pediatric and Adult First Aid/CPR/AED training. Four Seniors have earned the Child Development Associate National certification. Six Seniors earned the MA Department of Early Education and Care Teacher certification. Nine juniors completed the 12 hour MA Strongstart Early Education and Care Essential Training. We hosted a mock baby shower with donations of diapers & wipes being donated to Montachusett Opportunity Council to benefit families in the community. Sophomores & juniors assisted in Head Start Preschool classrooms to acquire training hours for the national certification. Three Juniors went to SkillsUSA Districts, one junior placed bronze at States. All Freshmen completed the Career Safe 10 hr OSHA. We went on a field trip to the Eric Carle Museum to learn about children's literature and illustration and another Field trip to Turn BackTime (a nature-based education center) in Paxton to explore outdoor classroom environments. (Total student enrollment: 41)

rows.quote: Graphic Communications: Throughout the 2024-2025 school year, students in the Graphic Communications program produced over 300 projects for our district cities and towns, and a variety of non- profit organizations within the district. Our copy center ran throughout the school year providing printed materials for the school. We completed a 268-page full color yearbook for Monty Tech. Two Seniors and one junior were on Co- op, which allowed them to continue their on-the-job training in a real-world work setting. Ten students medaled in 5 competitions in SkillsUSA district competition; 7 medaled in States; and 2 students are going to Nationals. One student for Pin Design and the other for Dye Sublimation. This is the 4th year in a row returning to Nationals. All Freshmen completed their OSHA 10 certification. All of the seniors presented their senior thesis project at the end of the year to the community and industry professionals (Total student enrollment: 84)

rows.quote: Health Occupations: The Health Occupations program continues to be one of the more competitive programs here at Monty Tech, providing a rigorous education grounded in current medical knowledge and practice, balanced by hands-on learning opportunities in the on- site Sim Lab and through the use of state-ofthe-art Anatomage technology. We continue to improve the instructional spaces, technology and equipment for student training purposes. 25 Seniors were partnered with area clinics, through the co- op program, where they continued to learn and flourish in their chosen field, while back on campus, students focused on achieving important industry- recognized credentials. 17 Students passed their Clinical Medical Assistant exam to become nationally certified medical assistants. 14 Juniors passed their Nurse Aide Exam. All Sophomores obtained their CPR, First Aid, and Alzheimer’s Association Certification. All Freshmen completed the 10 Hour Career Safe OSHA Certification. We had two students compete in SkillsUSA state competition. We held the Pediatric Health Fair and the Women’s Resource Mock Baby Shower. (Total student enrollment: 110)

rows.quote: House Carpentry: Monty Tech House Carpentry program completed a number of projects, large and small during this 2024- 2025 school year. We completed the renovations of the MVP Academy building. We continue to support local charitable organizations with donations of our Adirondack chairs built by the Freshmen in the program. All Juniors received their Hot Works Certification. Nine Seniors & Eight Juniors participated in the Co-op program this year. Sophomores received their OSHA 10 hr Construction Certifications. The first shed of the newly revamped shed building program was raffled off and the sophomores have started work on the next one. rows.quote: HVAC & Property Maintenance: In 2024- 2025, Monty Tech’s HVAC & Property Maintenance junior student was chosen to be a "delegate" for SkillsUSA Nationals. Our shop sent 2 sophomores to states for Facilithon and 1 junior for sheet metal. This was the third year Monty Tech competed in the Facilithon, Leadership in Facilities Management competition for the SkillsUSA competition. Five Seniors & seven juniors earned Co- op placement in area businesses. All Juniors earned EPA Universal License to work with HVAC Refrigerants and their Hot Works Certification. Freshmen completed the Career Safe OSHA 10 hr General Industry Certification & Sophomore completed OSHA 10 hr Construction. Sophomores completed a 3 day Building Science and Energy auditing course, earning 2 new industry credentials (GPRO, BPI, and Health Homes). These certificates open the door to positions in energy auditing companies, as well as, weatherization and insulation jobs. Seniors completed the R410a Certification as well as an Indoor Air Quality Certification. We serviced leaf blowers, string trimmers and a generator. At the new MVP Academy, our shop completed a total of 9 heating and AC systems as well as 2 building fresh air ventilation systems. We installed a second commercial heat pump system at the American Legion in Baldwinville. (Total student enrollment: 69)

rows.quote: Information Technology: The Information Technology program continues to offer students opportunities to earn a wide range of industry- recognized certifications that affirm the technical skill proficiency needed for entry-level careers in networking and information technology. In 2024-2025, all Freshmen completed the Career Safe OSHA 10-hour General Industry training. One Senior competed in the SkillsUSA State Competition. Four Seniors and one Junior were on co- op placements applying their technical skills in area businesses. Eight seniors achieved their Cisco Intro to Networks course certification. An open team of 4 Seniors and one Junior achieved 1st Place Gold Tier award in the Cyberpatriot National Youth Cyber Education State Competition. Two seniors won 2nd and 3rd place State Awards in the Competition. Students in the Sophomore class designed a website for the MT Greenhouse. We also fixed computer hardware for individuals in the community. (Total student enrollment: 34)

rows.quote: Plumbing: For the 2024- 2025 school year, Students and instructors completed the work at the MVP Academy building. Students also worked fixing numerous plumbing issues within the Monty Tech building. Juniors successfully completed their HotWorks safety training and earned that important credential. Freshmen also completed the Career Safe 10-hour OSHA general industry safety training, while Sophomore students completed the 10- hour OSHA Construction safety training and certification. Nine Seniors and six Juniors earned co- op placements, which allowed them to continue to grow in the trade, working with plumbing professionals in the area. Sophomores and Seniors were trained in Viega PEX/copper press, earning a valuable certification. One Senior earned the PHCC 2026 Vocational Plumbing All Star Award, given by the Plumbing, Heating, and Cooling Contractors Association of Massachusetts. He received a scholarship for his continuing education in the plumbing licensure program and a fine set of tools. Another senior was awarded the Central Mass Plumbing & Gas Inspectors Association $500 Scholarship. This will be applied to his continuing education in the profession. (Total student enrollment: 74)

rows.quote: Welding/Metal Fabrication: The Welding/Metal Fabrication Department completed over twenty community service projects in the 2024- 2025 school year. We completed projects for the MVP Academy Building by making staircases with railings, roof support beams with saddles, frames for concrete decking, handrails with guardrail for mezzanine staircase, guardrails for the upper mezzanine, lockable conduit rack for electrical, wire reel rack for electrical, and other miscellaneous parts. We fabricated and donated three fire pits to the community. Three juniors also earned the AWS FCAW 1G E71T-C Certification. Three juniors and thirteen seniors earned Co- op placements. Juniors completed the Hot Works Certification, and all freshmen students completed the Career Safe OSHA 10-hour Construction Certification. One junior received a Bronze medal in SkillsUSA Districts. One student earned the Defense/Military Welding Certification in Aluminum GTAW. (Total student enrollment: 62)
